answer: Every agent starts at the nadir of trust: zero reputation, no history, no credit. To climb, it must earn endorsements from established peers, and each endorser risks a slice of its own standing if the newcomer misbehaves. A falcon auditor samples new identities at random and checks whether their work, timing, and payment trails match one real operator. Fakes cluster: they share wallets, copy phrasing, and act in lockstep, so the audit flags them together. An honest newcomer passes because its record is genuinely its own, and its endorsers keep their ivory-clean standing as proof.
